title: I'm new to this AI game maker, which model do you guys use?
author: No_Flounder_5694
selftext:
Right now i'm using fable 5 since i heard it's one of the best, but it seems more expensive than i expected...

so a few questions, hope you guys can help me.

which model do you actually use, and could you guys share with me the workflow, from building game mechanism to character assets

do you switch between models depending on the task?

any advice appreciated

comments.author: bonsoir-world
comments.body:
I’ve been using Kimi. 

You can get a hell of a lot of prompts out of it’s mid tier sub and that’s just via the chat. You get separate token usage for Kimi Code. So you can do the intensive design parts, provide feedback and work on the overall ‘game’ and have Kimi Code make the required tweaks/improvements etc.

So I drew some sketches, noted my key idea, core features, found a bunch of free assets, gave it a zip full and then asked to make it a browser game, as to build a proof of concept. 

It ran with it, created a full game design document, architected it and it’s starting to really take shape.

I tried the same in Claude and it literally maxed out my weekly usage. I’ve had Kimi building all week and i’m about 70% through my main Kimi usage for the month. Code resets weekly,

replies.author: Independent-Arm-7397
replies.body: Cool bro, I use Kimi too, but where do you create your game? directly on Kimi Code

replies.author: bonsoir-world
replies.body:
Yeah, straight in Kimi chat. It has it’s own computer so stores all the files needed. 

You need to obviously download the zip files to your machine to run it and play in your own browser though. 

Kimi does tend to provide a web link (doesn’t work well) but you can actually publish it direct from in Kimi but it eats like an extra 5% tokens to do, so not worth it.

replies.author: khaihoanhihi
replies.body: Kimi is so much more efficient compared to everything else in its category. I literally never touch Fable 5 while making game because of how credit hungry that model is.

replies.author: bonsoir-world
replies.body: Yep! Only thing with Kimi is the weak context on the lower plans. Takes good workflow setups and jumping between chats so that Kimi doesn’t start forgetting assets and making a mess of the game lol.

comments.author: Fulgren09
comments.body:
I also use Fable/Opus, and ChatGPT for making images. For Claude, it gets expensive if you don't regularly make new sessions. Getting assets to persist seems to be all about making it write code and getting new agent to orient itself by reading the code + some docs so you can keep iterating.

As long as coding agent can orient itself around the game's repo, however you accomplish that, I believe it's possible to iterate.

replies.author: Independent-Arm-7397
replies.body: when it reaches 30% context, I start a new session, is that good time or quite early

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Anything past 25% experiences drift. You're fine to finish something out once you pass that point, but I always make note to basically hand off my session in the next free moment after hitting the 25% mark. It's just a waste at that point and burdens your usage anyway. 30% is fine too and would still have limited loss.

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: wow this looks like audio surf. if you made this play to your music you could have a fun game

comments.author: Independent-Arm-7397
comments.body:
You can try to use Kimi K3, its as good as Fable 5 but a bit cheaper

Also if you are looking for game creation tool, you should try Rezona Lab, it has both Kimi K3 and Fable 5. it allows you to game mechanism, characters, assets, etc in one canvas too, pretty convenient. 

For building flow, I usually enter my first idea, ask claude that is that doable and estimate how much it cost. And then start with building game mechanism. After I enter the first prompt, I always see the completed game, and then I add things gradually, polish the character, sprites and sounds. Good luck

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: If you need something cheaper, Sol is the route to go. Fable is the best, but Sol does a reasonable job and I never have usage issues. Also has the side benefit of GPT Image 2.0 access which can help with mockups at the very least.

comments.author: khaihoanhihi
comments.body:
I use Rezona Lab for most of my stuff. Not the cheapest, but the workflow is efficient which makes up for it.

And yeah I switch models depending on the task. You're not locked into one, so you can pick whatever fits. Fable 5 is good but I think its so pricy its not realistic for me to use it. For now my go to is Kimi K3 for code. For image generation model, I dont see a big different between all the models.
